meaning.name: Fill the cart and check out
meaning.purpose: The visitor or the customer, through the shop's pages, ends with the cart they want, a code applied, and the cart closed as the order's record when the order is placed.
meaning.steps: 1. The page asks for the cart; the caller's open cart is answered, made empty where there is none, each line saying whether its price changed since it was added. A1, R1, R10 2. The visitor adds a product, one to five; a sixth of it, a thirty-first product, or more than the stock is refused with its words. A2, R2 3. They set a line's quantity, and nought takes the line out. A3, R3 4. They take a product out. A4, R4 5. They type a code; it is applied in place of any before it, or refused with what is wrong. A5, R5 6. Every answer holds the totals, delivery free from €50 after the discount. A1, R6 7. Signed in, the customer places the order: orders closes the cart, which is kept as the order's record, or the cart refuses where it is empty or a line is beyond its stock; the next cart the page asks for is new and empty. A7, R8, R1

meaning.name: See the cart
meaning.statement: When the shop's pages ask for the caller's cart, the cart shall answer the caller's open cart, made empty where there is none, with each line, the count of every unit, the code applied with its percent, and the totals.

meaning.says: Given a visitor with no cart, when their page asks for the cart, then an empty open cart is answered, with a count of 0 and a total of €0.

Given a cart of 2 Volt 65 chargers and 1 Hush 700, when the page asks for it, then two lines are answered, each with its name, quantity, price when added, price now, whether it is in stock and its total, and the count is 3.
Given a customer signed in, when the page asks for the cart, then the account's cart is answered, not the cart of the session.
Given WELCOME10 applied, when the page asks for the cart, then the answer holds WELCOME10 and 10 percent beside the amount taken off.
Given a line whose product is gone from the catalogue, when the page asks for the cart, then the line is answered by its slug, with no price now and not in stock.
Given the customer's cart was checked out, when their page asks for the cart, then a new empty cart is answered.

meaning.name: Say when a line's price changed
meaning.statement: While the price now of a line's product differs from its price when added, the cart shall answer the line as changed, with both prices, and keep its total at the price when added.

meaning.says: Given a line of 1 Hush 700 added at €299.00 and its price now €279.00, when the cart is answered, then the line is marked changed, with €299.00 and €279.00, and its total is €299.00.
Given a line whose price has not changed, when the cart is answered, then the line is not marked changed.
Given a line whose product is gone from the catalogue, when the cart is answered, then the line is not marked changed and has no price now.

meaning.name: A code once per customer
meaning.statement: When a customer applies a code they used on an earlier order, the cart shall refuse it.

meaning.name: Add a product
meaning.statement: When a page adds a product to the cart in a quantity of one to five, the cart shall add it as a line at its price now, or raise the quantity of its line where the product is in the cart already.

meaning.says: Given an empty cart, when 2 Volt 65 chargers are added, then the cart holds one line of 2 at €39.00 and the count is 2.
Given the cart holds 2 Volt 65 chargers, when 1 more is added, then the line holds 3.
Given the cart holds 4 of a product, when 2 more are added, then the cart refuses with "up to 5 of each product" and is unchanged.
Given the cart holds thirty different products, when a thirty-first is added, then the cart refuses with "a cart holds up to 30 different products".
Given the Nomad 13 with 2 in stock, when 3 are added, then the cart refuses with "only 2 of Nomad 13 left".
Given the Zen 12 with none in stock, when it is added, then the cart refuses with "Zen 12 is out of stock".
Given a slug the catalogue does not have, when it is added, then the cart answers 404 with "no product has that slug".

meaning.name: Change a line's quantity
meaning.statement: When a page sets the quantity of a line, the cart shall set it to that number, from one to five and within the stock, and take the line out where the number is nought.

meaning.says: Given a line of 1 Hush 700, when its quantity is set to 3, then the line holds 3 and the count rises by 2.
Given a line of the Hush 700, when its quantity is set to 0, then the line is gone.
Given a line of the Nomad 13 with 2 in stock, when its quantity is set to 3, then the cart refuses with "only 2 of Nomad 13 left" and the line is unchanged.
Given a quantity of 6, when it is set, then it is refused and the line is unchanged.
Given a product that is not in the cart, when its quantity is set, then the cart answers 404 with "that product is not in the cart".

meaning.name: Take a product out
meaning.statement: When a page takes a product out of the cart, the cart shall remove its line and answer the cart without it.

meaning.says: Given a cart of the Hush 700 and a Volt 65 charger, when the Hush 700 is taken out, then the charger's line alone is left and the totals are the charger's.
Given a product that is not in the cart, when it is taken out, then the cart answers as it was, with no refusal.

meaning.name: Apply a discount code
meaning.statement: When a page applies a code, the cart shall read it without the spaces around it and in capitals, and apply it in place of any code before it, where it is four to twelve letters and digits, a code the shop runs, and not past its date.

meaning.says: Given a cart of the Hush 700 at €299.00, when "welcome10" is applied, then WELCOME10 is applied, €29.90 is taken off and the total is €269.10.
Given WELCOME10 is applied, when AUTUMN5 is applied, then AUTUMN5 alone is applied.
Given "no spaces" is typed, when it is applied, then the cart answers 422 with "a code is 4 to 12 letters and digits" and the code applied before stays.
Given "NOPE1" is typed, when it is applied, then the cart answers 422 with "that code is not known".
Given AUTUMN5 after 30 November 2026, when it is applied, then the cart answers 422 with "AUTUMN5 expired on 30 November 2026".
Given AUTUMN5 applied on 29 November 2026, when the cart is checked out on 2 December 2026, then AUTUMN5 still takes its 5 percent off.

meaning.name: Total the cart
meaning.statement: The cart shall total every cart it answers: the lines added, the code's percent of that taken off and rounded half up to the cent, delivery of €4.90 under €50 after the discount and none from €50 or on an empty cart, and their sum.

meaning.says: Given one Volt 65 charger at €39.00, when the cart is totalled, then delivery is €4.90 and the total €43.90.
Given two Volt 65 chargers at €78.00, when the cart is totalled, then delivery is €0 and the total €78.00.
Given lines of €52.00 and a code of 10 percent, when the cart is totalled, then €5.20 is taken off, €46.80 is under €50, delivery is €4.90 and the total €51.70.
Given an empty cart, when it is totalled, then every total is €0.
Given a cart orders has checked out, when orders asks its totals, then they are the totals the customer last saw.

meaning.name: Carry the visitor's cart at sign-in
meaning.statement: When accounts signs in a visitor whose cart holds a line, the cart shall carry the visitor's lines into the account's open cart, the larger quantity winning for a product in both, within five of a product and thirty products, and abandon the visitor's cart.

meaning.says: Given a visitor's cart of 3 Volt 65 chargers and an account's cart of 1 charger and 1 Hush 700, when the visitor signs in, then the account's cart holds 3 chargers and the Hush 700, and the visitor's cart is abandoned.
Given 2 of a product in the visitor's cart and 5 in the account's, when the visitor signs in, then the account's cart holds 5.

Given an account's cart of 29 products and a visitor's cart of 3 others, when the visitor signs in, then the account's cart holds 30 products: the first of the visitor's three is carried, and the other two are not.
Given an account with no open cart, when a visitor with 2 lines signs in, then the account has an open cart of those 2 lines.
Given a visitor's cart with no line, when they sign in, then the account's cart is unchanged.

meaning.name: Close the cart at checkout
meaning.statement: When orders checks out a cart that holds a line and whose every line is within its stock, the cart shall close it for good, as the order's record.

meaning.says: Given a cart of 1 Hush 700 with 8 in stock, when orders checks it out, then the cart is checked out and its lines and totals stay as they were.
Given a checked-out cart, when a product is added to it or a code applied, then the cart refuses with "this cart has been checked out; start a new one".
Given an empty cart, when orders checks it out, then the cart refuses with "the cart is empty" and stays open.
Given a line of 2 Nomad 13 and the stock fallen to 1, when orders checks the cart out, then the cart refuses with "nomad-13 is no longer in stock in that quantity" and stays open.

meaning.name: Let go of carts nobody touches
meaning.statement: When the nightly job runs, the cart shall abandon every open cart of a customer untouched for thirty days and every open cart of a visitor untouched for 48 hours, and answer how many it abandoned.

meaning.says: Given a customer's open cart last touched 31 days ago, when the nightly job runs, then it is abandoned and counted.
Given a customer's open cart last touched 29 days ago, when the nightly job runs, then it stays open.
Given a visitor's open cart last touched 49 hours ago, when the nightly job runs, then it is abandoned.
Given a visitor's open cart last touched 47 hours ago, when the nightly job runs, then it stays open.
Given a cart checked out a year ago, when the nightly job runs, then it stays checked out.

meaning.boundary: The cart is a part of the shop's back end, and this is its edge: what crosses it, both ways, and what stays on the other side. | What | Is | |---|---| | The whole | Voltline's back end: one service with a package per part, each its team's, mounted by platform under /api/v1 (E18, E76); the cart leaves it for a service of its own in January 2027 (E1) | | Comes in | the shop's pages' calls to the five routes under /api/v1/cart, with the session cookie, A1 to A5 (E22, E76); accounts' call at sign-in, A6 and A9 (E80); orders' calls at checkout, A7 and A10 (E89, E91); the nightly job's call, A8 (E68) | | Goes out | the cart as the pages read it: its lines with the price when added and the price now, the count, the discount, the subtotal, delivery and total, and the sum from which delivery is free (E21); a closed cart, whose lines and totals are the order's record (E88) | | Called by | the shop's pages, for the visitor and the customer; accounts, at sign-in; orders, at checkout; the nightly job (E5) | | Calls | the catalogue, for a product by its slug: its name, its price and its stock (E83); accounts, for the caller's session, which says whose cart it is (E22); the marketing team's codes, read (E56) | | Never | changes stock: the catalogue takes it, when orders asks (E66, E84); places an order: orders does (E17, E89); signs anyone in or makes a session: accounts does (E16, E79); writes a code: the codes are the marketing team's (E7, E56) | | Owns | N1 the cart, N2 its lines, N3 its discount (E19, E71) | | Refers to | N4 the product, owned by the catalogue team; N5 the customer, owned by the accounts team; N6 the order, owned by the orders team; each by its key alone (E15, E16, E17) |
meaning.journey: 1. A visitor adds products to the cart from the shop's pages; each call answers the whole cart, with its lines and totals. 2. They change a quantity, take a product out, and type a code into the code box; today 31 codes of 100 are refused here. 3. At the checkout they sign in; accounts carries the visitor's cart into the account's; today about 9 customers a week find it empty or changed here. 4. Orders places the order: it closes the cart, which is kept as the order's record, and reads the total. 5. A cart nobody touches is let go by the nightly job.
meaning.name: Voltline cart
meaning.non-goals: - A cart saved for later, or shared with someone else: not now, says the brief (E6). - Codes that stack: one code at a time, B4, stays as it is (E6, E7). - A code that may be used once per customer, R11: the marketing team's table does not know who used a code (E12). - The stock: the cart reads it and never changes it; taking stock is the catalogue's, at orders' call (E84). - How the split is built: this specification says what the cart answers, not how it is moved.
meaning.problem: The cart is being split out of the shop's one service, and nothing says today what the catalogue, accounts and orders teams can count on from it, or what the cart team may not touch (E1). Two things already go wrong, by the lead engineer's counts of September 2026: about 9 customers a week tell support that their cart was empty, or not what they had put in, after they signed in (E2); and 31 of every 100 codes typed into the cart's code box are refused, most for a space inside or a date passed (E3). The code shows what a customer meets at that moment: the visitor's lines join whatever the account's cart already held, kept up to thirty days, and of a product in both the larger quantity wins (E60, E68). Two of the cart's own limits are not held today: a visitor's cart is meant to live 48 hours and nothing holds it to that (X1), and a carried cart can pass thirty products (X3).
meaning.release plan: | Release | Holds | Outcome | |---|---|---| | First | R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8, R9 | the cart as its own service: the pages fill it, accounts carries it at sign-in, orders closes it, the nightly job lets old carts go | | Later | R10 | a line says when its price changed since it was added |
meaning.summary: The cart is the part of Voltline's back end that holds what a visitor or a customer has chosen to buy and not yet ordered: its lines, a discount code, and the totals the pages and the checkout show. This specification says what the cart does today, where it ends, and what it must never do, so that the cart can leave the shop's one service in January 2027 for a service of its own, owned by a new cart team, without breaking anything that calls it (E1). It is read from the code, its tests and the lead engineer's brief.
meaning.users: The cart has no screen of its own: people meet it through the shop's pages, and three parts of the back end call it (E5). The visitor: anyone on the shop without signing in, whose cart is kept by their session (U1). The customer: a visitor signed in, whose cart is kept by their account and follows them from one session to the next (U2). Accounts: the part that signs a visitor in, and carries their cart into the account's at that moment (U3). Orders: the part that places an order from a cart, closes the cart and reads its total (U4). The nightly job: what lets go, once a night, of the carts nobody has touched (U5).
